issues.legal_issue: A compromise decree in a partition suit is final when it allots specific properties and leaves no further inquiry or partition work to be done.
material_facts: The compromise specified the properties allotted to the participating parties and stated that they were in separate and exclusive possession of their respective properties.
The compromise contained no provision for further steps to partition the properties, and the court passed a decree in accordance with it.
issues.conclusion: The compromise decree was a final decree, not a preliminary decree, and no further final-decree proceeding was required to make it executable.
issues.legal_principle: A preliminary decree declares rights or shares while leaving further inquiry to be conducted; a final decree determines the rights completely. The court applied the distinction discussed in Rachakonda Venkat Rao v. R. Satya Bai and Renu Devi v. Mahendra Singh, and relied on Muzaffar Husain v. Sharafat Hussain and Raghubir Sahu v. Ajodhya Sahu for the treatment of a compromise decree that specifies allocations and requires no further inquiry. Order XXVI, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure applies after a preliminary partition decree where further partition work remains.

rule.if: partition_suit_decree and compromise_allocates_specific_properties and parties_already_in_exclusive_possession and no_further_partition_inquiry_required

predicates.partition_suit_decree: The court issued the decree in a proceeding seeking partition of property.
predicates.compromise_allocates_specific_properties: The parties' compromise identified the specific properties allotted to the respective parties.
predicates.parties_already_in_exclusive_possession: The compromise stated that the parties were already in separate and exclusive possession of their respective allotted properties.
predicates.no_further_partition_inquiry_required: The compromise left no further inquiry or partition work to be carried out.

issues.definition: When a partition decree based on a compromise specifies the allocations, the parties already possess their allotted properties separately, and nothing remains to be done, the decree is final and immediately executable.

issues.legal_issue: The limitation period for executing an immediately enforceable decree continues to run while a separate challenge to the decree is pending unless a court stays the decree or its operation.
material_facts: The compromise decree finally allotted property and was immediately executable.
A later suit challenged the decree, followed by an appeal, but no court stayed the decree or proceedings under it.
The execution application was filed more than twelve years after the decree became enforceable.
issues.conclusion: The execution proceeding was barred by limitation; the pending challenge did not suspend or extend the limitation period because no stay had been ordered.
issues.legal_principle: Article 136 of the Limitation Act provides a twelve-year period for execution of a civil court decree, running from when the decree becomes enforceable. Under Ratan Singh v. Vijay Singh, filing an appeal does not affect enforceability unless the appellate court stays the decree. Ram Bachan Rai v. Ram Udar Rai likewise treated execution as time-barred where proceedings challenging a decree remained pending without a stay. Dr. Chiranji Lal v. Hari Das explains that limitation cannot be postponed by a decree-holder's own act or by an event that does not prevent execution. The court also relied on Manohar v. Jaipalsing in considering the effect of an order that did not stay the decree.

rule.if: execution_proceeding and final_decree_immediately_enforceable and execution_filed_after_applicable_period and challenge_proceeding_pending and no_stay_order

predicates.execution_proceeding: A decree-holder filed an application seeking execution of a civil court decree.
predicates.final_decree_immediately_enforceable: The decree finally determined the parties' rights and could be executed when it was passed.
predicates.execution_filed_after_applicable_period: The execution application was filed after the applicable limitation period had elapsed from the date the decree became enforceable.
predicates.challenge_proceeding_pending: A separate proceeding challenging the decree remained pending during some or all of the limitation period.
predicates.no_stay_order: No court ordered a stay of the decree or of proceedings to execute it.

issues.definition: When execution of a final decree is sought after the applicable limitation period, a pending challenge does not prevent the application from being time-barred if no court stayed the decree.
